Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (throughput / latency)

Thanks for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and agreed next steps on performance/SLOs and throughput sizing so we can scope a trial environment: 

Summary of what you shared
- Primary use case: policy-enforcement assistant integrated into Finex's customer support UI.
- Typical response sizes: 150-500 tokens (median ~220).
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~120 rps of inference calls during business hours.
- Peak traffic: up to 3x steady (bursty around product launches) — short spikes to ~360 rps lasting ~30-90 minutes.
- Streaming requirement: yes — need chunked/streaming output for progressive rendering of responses.
- Latency target: P95 < 250ms for 512-token responses (including initial token).

What we (Redwood) will validate
- Baseline throughput and latency for the selected model/quantization profile (P95/P99).
- Concurrency needed to hit 120 rps steady with headroom for bursts to 360 rps.
- Streaming behavior: tokens/sec and end-to-end time to first token for the client integration.

Next steps (owner)
1) Finex: share sample payloads and representative prompt sets (Alice) -- please drop finex_sample_payloads.csv into the Drive link.
2) Redwood: Rafael to produce an initial throughput estimate and recommended sizing (Rafael) -- includes tokens/sec, expected QPS, and concurrency guidance.
3) Schedule a short load-test window once payloads are shared -- propose week of Aug 17.

Attachments: finex_sample_payloads.csv (placeholders okay), throughput-modeling-notes.xlsx (we'll attach our baseline worksheet), redwood_arch_diagram.pdf (how we handle streaming + KV cache).

Let me know if I missed anything.

Hi all — following up with initial sizing and assumptions based on the numbers Neha/Alice shared. This is an initial estimate; we'll refine after we see the sample payload distribution and run a short load test.

Assumptions
- Model/config: Llama-2-13B (quantized FP16/INT8 mix) -- we'll map exact model once Finex confirms quality constraints.
- Median response length: 220 tokens; 95th percentile ~512 tokens; tail up to ~900 tokens (2%).
- Network: 99ms RTT included in baseline (adjustable by region).

Sizing estimates (steady vs peak)
- Steady-state: 120 rps * 220 tokens = 26,400 tokens/sec.
- Peak bursts: 360 rps * 220 tokens = 79,200 tokens/sec (if all median).
- If many requests hit 512 tokens, peak token/sec could approach ~184,320 tokens/sec (360 * 512).

Latency/Concurrency guidance
- To meet P95 < 250ms for 512-token generation is aggressive; for streaming-first-token targets, aim for first-token P95 < 200ms and tail completion within 1s for 512 tokens (streamed).
- Concurrency: estimate ~12 concurrent model instances (active in-flight requests) to handle 120 rps with low queuing when using batching-friendly runtime and KV caching; for peak 360 rps plan for ~36 concurrency instances. These map to X GPUs depending on model (I'll map to GPU counts after we pick the exact model).

Streaming specifics
- For progressive rendering we recommend chunked streaming with 64-token flushes; effective tokens/sec served per stream will depend on batching (we can sustain higher aggregate tokens/sec by batching across streams).
- First byte latency is primarily dominated by scheduling + model startup for that request; with prewarmed workers and prefix cache we expect first byte within 120-180ms in our tests for prioritized traffic.

Next steps
1) Finex to upload sample payloads and flag a representative set of long prompts (Alice).
2) Rafael to run tabletop config mapping to GPUs/quantization and send a recommended Dedicated trial size (I will attach throughput-modeling-notes.xlsx).
3) Schedule 2-hour load test window (Tues/Wed preferred) -- Rafael/Marissa to own execution; Neha to confirm times with Finex.

Attachments: throughput-modeling-notes.xlsx (baseline workbook). I'll also attach redwood_arch_diagram.pdf showing streaming and KV cache flow.

-- Rafael
